Under "alternatives", I would prefer that sole responsibility for the jurisdiction of the proposed legislation be vested in the Department of Interior rather than designating partial jurisdiction for some marine species to the Sécretary of Commercia. It may be very difficult for an agency whose primary mission is exploitive to take effective action for protection of endangered species in cases where such action may involve actual or imagined conflict with commercial harvesting of these or other species.
One of the potential drawbacks of the proposed legislation is that giving primary authority for protection of endangered or potentially endangered species and subspecies to the Federal Government might inhibit research on management of those form by state conservation agencies. Even though the proposed act provides for state input into the process, the red tape involved, inter agency jealousies, and possible conflicts of interest could in some cases actually work to the detriment of the species of wildlife involved. Hopefully, all agencies involved will work together in good faith to accomplish the objectives of the proposed legislation.
I feel that one of the major faults of the proposed legisla-, tion is its failure to emphasize the absolute necessity for additional recearch on endangered and potentially en-.dangered wildlife and to provide moneys for such activity. In a vast number of cases, there is not enough scientific information about particular wildlife species to provide a balis for a decision on the status of their populations. Therefore, setting up criteria for endangered or potentially endangered categories and means of protecting organisms so identified would be more useful if provision was also made to allow an accurate determination of which populations actually belong in these cutegories and to provide the basic data on their ecology and life history necessary for effective action to preserve them. I also strongly feel that a significant share of financial support for research on endangered or potentially entangered wildlife should be channeled directly to an retriate state conservation agencies, universities, or other ton-governmental scientific organizations in the form of grants or contracts. In many cases this approach can provide a more effective and efficient means of obtaining the kind of basic scientific data needed than by expansion of Pederal programs.
